items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: In those days, my idol was Earl Hines.

ctx.x: Could I sort of break in here. We've really gotten charged ahead time-wise, I'd like to get back. It's easy to do that. I'd still like to talk a little bit about musical things, even back when you were still at Wilberforce and thereafter. The piano style that you were playing in those days -- was this basically oriented to the stride bass kind of piano?

In those days, my idol was Earl Hines. And I used to watch Fatha whenever I had the chance, you know, because I would see him quite a bit, and he and my brother were very good friends, and they would sit down and talk music, and Earl would play. He loved to play a jam session and things, you know. And this particular 'Sweet Lorraine' (unintelligible) was his bag, deal even in those days. And I don't think of a day now even when I play 'Sweet Lorraine,' (unintelligible) that I don't think of Earl Hines. But he had…

you know, if you don't, you be (unintelligible), you know? And I just admired the man, you know, and I always loved him, and in fact, as you know, Earl is from Duquesnes, Pennsylvania. And my band was booked in Pittsburgh, even though I was in school, you know. We played Pittsburgh in the summer. And Earl was playing around there, and in those days, there were a lot of jam sessions, and they weren't restricted by the local, you know, like they used to find guys for sitting in, and all those kind of things.
